forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

summary.summary: Fareham's Annual Governance Statement 2025/26 comes to committee for approval ahead of publication with the Statement of Accounts. The covering report confirms the requirement to publish a draft AGS alongside the draft accounts in June was met, and says the improvements identified by the annual review 'do not necessarily signify a significant control weakness' but reflect ideas for refining existing processes. Nothing in the paper points to financial or governance distress; external assurance sources reviewed include the 2024/25 external audit completion report. The AGS itself (Appendix D) is a separate attachment, so this record is grounded on the covering report and its appendices A-B only.

signals.headline: AGS 2025/26 on schedule — the June draft-publication requirement was met and the governance review identified no significant control weaknesses, only process improvements (pages 2-3)
signals.why: A clean, on-time governance statement supports confidence in the council's control environment; nothing here alarms a lender.

news_drafts.headline: Fareham Council anticipates a 2026/27 underspend and a contribution to reserves
news_drafts.lead:
Fareham Borough Council set its 2026/27 budget without drawing on its reserves, the money it has put aside. The latest budget monitoring report, the in-year check of spending against budget, goes to the Executive. It says any underspend will be added to general fund reserves, and that it is anticipated the year will end in underspend, "which will mean there would be a contribution to reserves". The paper adds that spending tends to rise in the later months of the year.

Two income lines are above budget to 30 September 2026. Planning applications income is almost £130k above budget, which the paper attributes mainly to an increase in major applications that bring larger fees. This is partly offset by higher employee costs. Car park income is £102k above budget, which the paper attributes to higher town centre and coastal parking levels. An underspend on business rates has also helped that service, partly offset by higher maintenance costs.

The housing revenue account (HRA), the separate account for the council's own housing, paid for by rents, shows a surplus of £4.423m transferred to the HRA reserve at 30 September. That is £76k above the £4.347m budgeted for the first six months. Income is £171k above the half-year budget, mainly from 2025/26 service charge adjustments and a Council Housebuilding Support grant rolled forward. The paper says the surplus does not yet reflect year-end corporate recharges and reserve adjustments. It says the full-year forecast outturn, the actual figures once the year has ended, is expected to be in line with budget.

findings.headline: Disabled Facilities Grants spend was £187,912 against a £400,000 budget to 30 September 2026, with a delay in invoicing for the second quarter.
findings.detail: Applications are processed by Portsmouth City Council on Fareham's behalf, with some small house clearance works managed in-house. The paper names the invoicing delay as the reason the spend is low against the profiled budget.
findings.matters: Delegated processing through a neighbouring council means invoicing timing can hold back reported capital spend, which affects shared-service arrangements elsewhere.
findings.figures: £1,310,200 scheme budget; £400,000 budget to 30 Sep 26; £187,912 actual to 30 Sep 26
findings.quote: There has been a delay in invoicing for the second

findings.headline: The National Lottery Heritage Fund has approved the continuation of Holly Hill Rediscovered and the requested budget uplift.
findings.detail: The project is progressing to RIBA Stage 4 (Construction) after the Landscape Architect was reappointed. The paper says the Fund continues to commend the way the Council is managing and delivering the project.
findings.matters: External grant funder approval of a budget uplift is the kind of outcome other councils running heritage-funded schemes will want to know about.
findings.figures: £2,044,803 scheme budget; £358,800 added to scheme budget in February 2026
findings.quote: The National Lottery Heritage Fund (NLHF) has approved both the continuation of the project and the requested budget uplift.

findings.headline: The fair value of the Council's 10 commercial investment properties fell by £1,605,000 since 2025, with five properties rising in value and five falling.
findings.detail: The overall property portfolio, including the commercial properties, fell by £1,862,000 over the same period. The paper describes fluctuations as market sentiment rather than actual gains or losses. Contracted income is estimated at £4.1 million in 2026/27.
findings.matters: Falls in commercial property fair value affect the income and asset position of any council with a commercial property portfolio, and lenders track this exposure.
findings.figures: £1,605,000 decrease in fair value; £1,862,000 overall portfolio decrease; £33,825k value at 31 March 2025 to £32,220k at 31 March 2026; £4.1 million contracted income 2026/27
findings.quote: Since 2025 the Fair Value of the portfolio has decreased by £1,605,000.

findings.headline: Treasury management investments earned a net rate of return of 1.4% to 30 September 2026, against a 2.9% estimate, while commercial investments earned 4.4% against 3.6%.
findings.detail: The rate of return indicator is net of associated costs and shows the half-year position. The paper does not give a reason for the difference from the estimate.
findings.matters: A treasury return running below estimate at the half-year point is a figure finance directors will check against their own investment income forecasts.
findings.figures: Treasury management investments: 2.9% estimate, 1.4% actual to 30 Sept; Commercial investments: 3.6% estimate, 4.4% actual to 30 Sept; Total: 3.4% estimate, 3.5% actual

findings.headline: £12 million invested in strategic pooled funds returned an average total return of 5.10% to 30 September 2026, comprising a 4.49% income return.
findings.detail: The paper says the income return is used to support services in year. It adds 0.62% of unrealised capital gains. The investment table shows a pooled fund balance of £10,913k, and Appendix B refers to £11 million.
findings.matters: A council drawing a 4.49% income return from strategic funds to support services is a choice that other councils with similar investments will compare against cash returns.
findings.figures: £12 million in pooled funds (para 26); £10,913k balance at 30 Sept 2026; 5.10% average total return; 4.49% income return; 0.62% unrealised capital gains; £11 million (Appendix B)
findings.quote: These funds generated an average total return of 5.10%, comprising a 4.49% income return
